data.narrative:
First Light Fusion, a Series C nuclear energy company founded by Nicholas Hawker and Yiannis Ventikos, has raised over $100M to date. The nuclear energy sector includes 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private competitors such as Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and Fuse Energy, though a direct same-stage comparable set remains sparse.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach, using the company's $100M total raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $170M. A peer-median approach cannot be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow nuclear energy segment—only five sector peers exist, and filtering by stage and valuation tier yields fewer than the three datapoints required for statistical confidence.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $144M (low) to $195M (high), with a median of $170M. This range reflects the applicability of a single triangulation method and assumes the $100M raised proxy reasonably approximates recent post-money valuation. Key uncertainties include the absence of true peer multiples in the nuclear energy subsector at Series C, the proprietary nature of First Light's technology, and the regulatory trajectory of the fusion/fission hybrid segment. A full re-triangulation becomes feasible upon Series D or public comparable emergence.
